questions.q: Define "partial reinforcement effect" in one sentence using the terms "resistance to extinction" and "intermittent schedule".
questions.a: The partial reinforcement effect is the phenomenon where a response acquired under an intermittent (partial) schedule of reinforcement shows **greater resistance to extinction** than a response acquired under continuous reinforcement. A wrong answer that says "partial reinforcement makes learning faster" reveals confusion between **acquisition speed** (faster under continuous) and **persistence after reinforcement stops** (greater under partial).

questions.q: A teacher praises a student **only when the student raises her hand before speaking**. The student now raises her hand more often. Is the praise a positive reinforcer, negative reinforcer, or punisher? Justify in two sentences.
questions.a: The praise is a **positive reinforcer** because a **pleasant stimulus is added** contingent on the behaviour, and the behaviour **increases** in frequency. A wrong answer calling it "negative reinforcement" reveals the common misconception that "negative" means "bad" rather than "removal of a stimulus"; negative reinforcement would require removing something aversive (e.g., stopping a loud noise) to increase hand-raising.

questions.q: A factory pays piece-rate wages: ₹50 for every 10 garments stitched (fixed-ratio 10). Sketch the expected **response-rate pattern** (high/low, steady/burst-pause) and explain why a **variable-ratio 10** schedule would produce a steadier, higher rate.
questions.a: Fixed-ratio 10 produces a **"break-and-run" pattern**: a post-reinforcement pause followed by a rapid burst of stitching until the next 10 garments. Variable-ratio 10 eliminates the predictable pause because the worker never knows which garment will trigger payment, so responding stays **high and steady** (like a slot machine). A wrong answer claiming FR produces steadier responding confuses the **predictability** of the ratio requirement with the **unpredictability** of VR.

questions.q: Compare **fixed-interval 5 min** and **variable-interval 5 min** schedules in terms of (a) response pattern near the interval end, (b) overall response rate, and (c) resistance to extinction. Use a table.
questions.a:
| Feature | FI 5 min | VI 5 min |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Pattern near interval end | Scalloped: low early, accelerating near 5 min | Steady, moderate throughout |
| (b) Overall rate | Lower (long pauses) | Higher (no predictable safe period) |
| (c) Resistance to extinction | Moderate | Highest among interval schedules |
A wrong answer stating FI produces higher overall rates misses that the **long post-reinforcement pause** in FI depresses the average rate compared to VI’s steadiness.

questions.q: A parent shouts at a teenager each time the teen leaves dirty dishes in the sink. The teen **continues leaving dishes**. Evaluate whether the shouting functions as punishment, negative reinforcement, or neither. What change would make it effective punishment?
questions.a: The shouting is **neither punishment nor negative reinforcement** for dish-leaving because the target behaviour **did not decrease** (punishment) nor increase via escape/avoidance (negative reinforcement). It is simply an ineffective aversive stimulus. To make it punishment, the parent must ensure the shouting **immediately follows** the behaviour, is **sufficiently intense**, and is **consistently applied**—or replace it with response-cost (e.g., deducting pocket money) that reliably reduces the behaviour. A wrong answer calling it "punishment because it's unpleasant" ignores the **definitional requirement** that punishment must **suppress the response**.

questions.q: Design a **token-economy system** for a Class 11 study group that uses a **variable-ratio schedule** to maintain daily revision habits. Specify: (a) target behaviour, (b) token delivery rule, (c) backup reinforcer, (d) why VR is better than FR for long-term maintenance.
questions.a: (a) Target: completing 30 min of focused revision per subject daily. (b) Token rule: after each 30-min block, draw a chit from a box containing 10 chits—3 say "Token", 7 say "Try Again" (VR ≈ 3.3). (c) Backup reinforcer: 5 tokens = 1 hour of guilt-free gaming / ₹50 canteen coupon. (d) VR prevents the **post-reinforcement pause** seen in FR (where students would stop after earning a token) and creates **high, steady responding** with strong resistance to extinction when tokens are eventually faded. A poor answer that uses FR ("token every day") misses the **maintenance advantage** of unpredictability emphasized in NCERT's partial reinforcement effect.
